text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.
- Croatia and Yugoslavia start talks on regulating social security on an international level in line with the normalization agreement signed between the two countries.
- War invalids whose disability has been put at 100 percent to receive flats by March of 1997.
- Church and civil weddings to become equal, while permits become necessary for underage weddings.
- Croatia has spend more than one billion dollars from its budget on caring for refugees and displaced people during the war.
- Some 3,065 railway workers on strike might not receive their November pay, according to the Croatian railways general manager, Marijan Klaric.
- State incentive for agriculture and fishing: Some 570 million kuna set aside to ensure that farming land is not abandoned.
- Changes to the law on income tax: The meagre wages to experience a meagre increase of some four to six percent or in terms of actual wages, some 100 to 200 kuna.

- The chairman of the Kaptol Banka executive board, Dejan Kosutic is announcing that apart from the recent investment fund it had opened, the bank is planning to open a privatisation investment fund, but not before the start of coupon privatisation.
- Levi's investigators in action: Two months suspended sentence received by a vendor of counterfit Levi's jeans in Donji Miholjac.

- According to Wall Street Journal's assessment of investment opportunities in Central Europe, Croatia's positive sides are good companies and growing post-war economy, while it's drawbacks are low liquidity.
- Teachers' salaries to go up 17 percent in 1997, says in an interview deputy finance minister, Mijo Jukic. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
